arxiv-2107-10928.title: Kinetics of Carbon Condensation in Detonation of High Explosives: First-Order Phase Transition Theory Perspective
arxiv-2107-10928.creator: Apoorva Purohit, Kirill A. Velizhanin
arxiv-2107-10928.description: Abstract The kinetics of carbon condensation, or carbon clustering, in detonation of carbon-rich high explosives is modeled by solving a system of rate equations for concentrations of carbon particles. Unlike previous efforts, the rate equations account not only for the aggregation of particles, but also for their fragmentation in a thermodynamically consistent manner.

arxiv-2208-03533.title: Pattern alternations induced by nonlocal interactions
arxiv-2208-03533.creator: Swadesh Pal, Roderick Melnik, Malay Banerjee
arxiv-2208-03533.description: Abstract Pattern formation is a visual understanding of the dynamics of complex systems. Patterns arise in many ways, such as the segmentation of animals, bacterial colonies during growth, vegetation, chemical reactions, etc. In most cases, the long-range diffusion occurs, and the usual reaction-diffusion (RD) model can not capture such phenomena.

arxiv-2409-17531.title: SimVG: A Simple Framework for Visual Grounding with Decoupled Multi-modal Fusion
arxiv-2409-17531.creator: Ming Dai, Lingfeng Yang, Yihao Xu, Zhenhua Feng, Wankou Yang
arxiv-2409-17531.description: Abstract Visual grounding is a common vision task that involves grounding descriptive sentences to the corresponding regions of an image. Most existing methods use independent image-text encoding and apply complex hand-crafted modules or encoder-decoder architectures for modal interaction and query reasoning. However, their performance significantly drops when dealing with complex textual expressions.

arxiv-2410-10091.title: Out-of-Bounding-Box Triggers: A Stealthy Approach to Cheat Object Detectors
arxiv-2410-10091.creator: Tao Lin, Lijia Yu, Gaojie Jin, Renjue Li, Peng Wu ✉, Lijun Zhang ✉
arxiv-2410-10091.description: Abstract In recent years, the study of adversarial robustness in object detection systems, particularly those based on deep neural networks (DNNs), has become a pivotal area of research. Traditional physical attacks targeting object detectors, such as adversarial patches and texture manipulations, directly manipulate the surface of the object.

arxiv-2501-07795.title: Black-box Optimization with Simultaneous Statistical Inference for Optimal Performance
arxiv-2501-07795.creator: Teng Lian, Jian-Qiang Hu, Yuhang Wu, Zeyu Zheng
arxiv-2501-07795.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Teng Lian, Jian-Qiang Hu, Yuhang Wu, Zeyu Zheng. Black-box optimization is often encountered for decision-making in complex systems management, where the knowledge of system is limited. Under these circumstances, it is essential to balance the utilization of new information with computational efficiency. In practice, decision-makers often face the dual tasks of optimization and statistical inference for the optimal performance, in order to achieve it with a high reliability. Our goal is to address the dual tasks in an online fashion.

arxiv-2503-14555.title: A Generalist Hanabi Agent
arxiv-2503-14555.creator: Arjun Vaithilingam Sudhakar Hadi Nekoei Mathieu Reymond, Janarthanan Rajendran Miao Liu Sarath Chandar
arxiv-2503-14555.description: Abstract Traditional multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) systems can develop cooperative strategies through repeated interactions. However, these systems are unable to perform well on any other setting than the one they have been trained on, and struggle to successfully cooperate with unfamiliar collaborators.

arxiv-2504-02883.title: SemEval-2025 Task 4: Unlearning sensitive content from Large Language Models
arxiv-2504-02883.creator: Anil Ramakrishna, Yixin Wan, Xiaomeng Jin, Kai-Wei Chang, Zhiqi Bu, Bhanukiran Vinzamuri, Volkan Cevher, Mingyi Hong, Rahul Gupta
arxiv-2504-02883.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Anil Ramakrishna, Yixin Wan, Xiaomeng Jin, Kai-Wei Chang, Zhiqi Bu, Bhanukiran Vinzamuri, Volkan Cevher, Mingyi Hong, Rahul Gupta. We introduce SemEval-2025 Task 4: unlearning sensitive content from Large Language Models (LLMs). The task features 3 subtasks for LLM unlearning spanning different use cases: (1) unlearn long form synthetic creative documents spanning different genres; (2) unlearn short form synthetic biographies containing personally identifiable information (PII), including fake names, phone number, SSN, email and home addresses, and (3) unlearn real documents sampled from the target model’s

arxiv-2505-18188.title: Improving Generative Inverse Design of Rectangular Patch Antennas with Test Time Optimization
arxiv-2505-18188.creator: Beck LaBash, Shahriar Khushrushahi, Fabian Ruehle
arxiv-2505-18188.description: Abstract We propose a two-stage deep learning framework for the inverse design of rectangular patch antennas. Our approach leverages generative modeling to learn a latent representation of antenna frequency response curves and conditions a subsequent generative model on these responses to produce feasible antenna geometries.

arxiv-2506-22285.title: Revision of conservative lower bound on intergalactic magnetic field from Fermi and Cherenkov telescope observations of extreme blazars
arxiv-2506-22285.creator: Jeffrey Blunier 1, Andrii Neronov 1,2, Dmitri Semikoz 1
arxiv-2506-22285.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Jeffrey Blunier 1, Andrii Neronov 1,2, Dmitri Semikoz 1. Joint observations of extreme blazars with Fermi Large Area Telescope (LAT) and Imaging Atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes (IACT) have been previously used to derive lower bounds on intergalactic magnetic field (IGMF). We update these previous bounds using a set of extreme blazars that are detected in the Very-High-Energy (VHE, photon energies above 100 GeV) band by both Fermi/LAT and IACTs.

arxiv-2509-24253.title: MRAG-Suite: A Diagnostic Evaluation Platform for Visual Retrieval-Augmented Generation
arxiv-2509-24253.creator: Yuelyu Ji
arxiv-2509-24253.description: Abstract Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation (Visual RAG) significantly advances question answering by integrating visual and textual evidence. Yet, current evaluations fail to systematically account for query difficulty and ambiguity. We propose MRAG-Suite, a diagnostic evaluation platform integrating diverse multimodal benchmarks (WebQA, Chart-RAG, Visual-RAG, MRAG-Bench). We introduce difficulty-based and ambiguity-aware filtering strategies, alongside MM-RAGChecker, a claim-level diagnostic tool.

pmc-10477077.title: Reliability and Validity of the Korean Version of the Gout Impact Scale
pmc-10477077.creator: Min Jung Kim, Ju Yeon Kim, Jennifer Jooha Lee, Ki Won Moon, Kichul Shin
pmc-10477077.description: BackgroundThe Gout Impact Scale (GIS), part of the Gout Assessment Questionnaire 2.0, measures gout-specific health-related quality of life (HRQOL). This study aimed to translate the GIS into Korean and validate the Korean version (K-GIS) using generic HRQOL measures.MethodsThe GIS was translated into Korean and back-translated into English.

pmc-11296804.title: OCTS-07 TRIAL IN PROGRESS: PHASE II STUDY OF RADIATION THERAPY FOLLOWED BY INTRATHECAL TRASTUZUMAB/PERTUZUMAB IN THE MANAGEMENT OF HER2+ BREAST LEPTOMENINGEAL DISEASE

pmc-11296804.description: BACKGROUNDHER2+ leptomeningeal disease (LMD) has a poor prognosis with a high unmet clinical need. A previous phase I/II study revealed intrathecal (IT) trastuzumab to be well tolerated with improved overall survival (OS) compared to historical controls in HER2+ breast LMD. Radiotherapy can improve the flow of IT therapy through the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and provide symptomatic relief.

pmc-11710139.title: Evaluating Congruence Between Clinical and Biological Staging Across The Alzheimer’s Disease Spectrum
pmc-11710139.creator: Hussein Zalzale, Marina Scop Madeiros, Carolina Soares, Guilherme Bauer‐Negrini, Guilherme Povala, Pamela C.L. Ferreira, Livia Amaral, Firoza Z Lussier, Bruna Bellaver, Sarah Abbas, Matheus Scarpatto Rodrigues, Dana Tudorascu, Markley Oliveira, Cynthia Felix, Douglas Teixeira Leffa, Cécile Tissot, C
pmc-11710139.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundThe newly proposed criteria by the AA working group incorporates both biological and clinical stages to characterize the progression of AD. In this study, we aim to evaluate the agreement between these two complementary systems.MethodsUsing 188 participants from McGill TRIAD and 139 from the HEAD cohorts, we categorized participants into biological (0‐4) and clinical (0‐4) stages using amyloid PET, tau PET(MK‐6240), and clinical measures as described by the working group.

pmc-11714517.title: Public data tracing: A novel method for retrospectively collecting occupational data for brain bank research donors
pmc-11714517.creator: Rachel C Otte, Lauren Etter, Elliot I Surovell, Sarah Lim, Aly Pfaff, Amanda DeWitt, Jessica Sharrow, Shahriar Salamat, Megan L Zuelsdorff, Robert A Rissman, Barbara B Bendlin, Amy JH Kind, W Ryan Powell
pmc-11714517.description: BackgroundWorking conditions and contexts may influence the development of Alzheimer’s Disease and related dementias (ADRD), exposing individuals to modifiable risk factors across their life. Measurement of ADRD pathology at autopsy provides a gold standard outcome for evaluating the effects of lifetime exposures, but approaches to quantify ante‐mortem work exposures are limited.

pmc-12417947.title: Microglial voltage-gated proton channel 1 ablation in diabetic mice mitigates diabetes-driven demyelination and cognitive decline
pmc-12417947.creator: Bin Li
pmc-12417947.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). This article discusses a study by Li et al, which investigates the role of the microglial voltage-gated proton channel 1 (Hv1) in diabetes-related cognitive decline. The authors showed that Hv1 is upregulated in the corpus callosum of diabetic mice and that its knockout improves working memory, reduces microglial production of interleukin-1β and tumour necrosis factor alpha, and decreases apoptosis of oligodendrocyte progenitor cells.

This study investigates the relationship between baseline HbA1c levels, HbA1c trajectories, and hypertension risk.MethodsThis retrospective cohort study included 10,138 adults from health screenings at Henan Provincial People’s Hospital (January 2018–January 2025). Mean age was 54.03 ± 12.97 years, with 31.

pmc-13036486.title: Reversible RNA ADP-ribosylation on uracil bases
pmc-13036486.creator: Yang Lu, Li Tang, Øyvind Strømland, Chatrin Chatrin, Kang Zhu, Deeksha Munnur, Joséphine Groslambert, Petra Mikolčević, Herwig Schüler, Gyula Timinszky, Guillaume Gabant, Marcin J Suskiewicz, Andreja Mikoč, Vincent Aucagne, Dragana Ahel, Qiang Liu, Ivan Ahel
pmc-13036486.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ADP-ribosylation is a conserved modification that uses NAD+ as a co-substrate to regulate essential cellular processes, such as genome stability and transcription, with Poly(ADP-ribose) Polymerases (PARPs) serving as the major catalyzing enzymes in humans. Historically defined as a protein post-translational modification, ADP-ribosylation on nucleic acids has been increasingly recognized in recent years, particularly in bacterial systems, but remains poorly understood in higher organisms.

pmc-13121629.title: Elucidating genetic backgrounds of myasthenia gravis in Japanese by genome-wide association studies and multi-omics analyses of thymoma
pmc-13121629.creator: Hiroyuki Ueda, Tomoya Kubota, Risa Goto, Akari Suzuki, Takafumi Ojima, Kotaro Ogawa, Kyuto Sonehara, Shinichi Namba, Tatsuhiko Naito, Qingbo Wang, Shingo Konno, Makoto Samukawa, Naoki Kawaguchi, Takashi Kimura, Takamichi Sugimoto, Hiroyuki Murai, Takemori Yamawaki, Kenichi Kaida, Daiki Tokuyasu, Man
pmc-13121629.description: Myasthenia gravis (MG) is an autoimmune disorder characterized by impaired neuromuscular transmission and motor symptoms. Its genetic background remains unclear, particularly beyond specific subtypes reported in European populations. Here, we perform a genome-wide association study (GWAS) of 1,434 MG cases covering all disease subtypes and 42,913 controls of Japanese, which newly identify the TERT locus (odds ratio [OR] = 1.

pmc-13242836.title: Hydrocelectomy Complication Rates in the United States
pmc-13242836.creator: Dennis J Head, Jay D Raman, Roderick K Clark
pmc-13242836.description: Introduction and ObjectivesHydrocelectomy is the gold standard treatment for hydrocele. European data showed complication rates between 16% and 25%, however the rate within the United States has not been assessed. We examined the postoperative complication, emergency department visit, readmission and re-operation rates after hydrocelectomy in the United States.

pmc-13249738.title: Adapting to Modernity. River Engineering and Emotional Engineering in 1950s Sweden
pmc-13249738.creator: Fabian Zimmer
pmc-13249738.description: In the mid-1950s, Vattenfall, the Swedish State Power Board, faced a severe acceptance crisis. In the postwar years, Vattenfall had become one of the main drivers of Sweden’s technological modernization through electrification and the exploitation of hydropower resources in Northern Sweden.

pmc-13326622.title: Evaluation of the accuracy, consistency, and scientific reliability of AI-powered Chatbots in endodontic practice
pmc-13326622.creator: Saba Kilimci, Elif Delve Başer Can, Jale Tanalp
pmc-13326622.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectiveThis study aimed to evaluate the accuracy, consistency, and scientific reliability of two AI-powered chatbots—ChatGPT-3.5 and ChatGPT-4o—in clinical endodontic decision-making, using the recently published European Society of Endodontology (ESE) S3-level Clinical Practice Guideline as the gold standard reference.Material and MethodsTwenty-five dichotomous (yes/no) questions were developed based on the ESE guideline and presented to both chatbots across three time intervals, yielding 300 total responses.

pmc-13385755.title: Measuring the optimistic bias of cross-validation in radiomics
pmc-13385755.creator: Aydin Demircioğlu
pmc-13385755.description: In radiomics, independent external data are often unavailable and cross-validation (CV) schemes are widely used to obtain performance estimates. Simple k-fold CV is preferred over nested CV due to its lower computational cost, although nested CV is known to provide more accurate estimates.

pmc-13416527.title: Non-invasive mechanical ventilation as an adjunct to pulmonary rehabilitation in patients with bronchiectasis: a pathophysiological perspective
pmc-13416527.creator: Jhojan Sebastian Herrera-Vargas, Cristian Jose Gomez-Vega
pmc-13416527.description: Bronchiectasis is a complex respiratory disease characterized by irreversible bronchial dilatation, mucus hypersecretion, and impaired mucociliary clearance. These structural changes result in a predominantly obstructive pattern that increases airway resistance, impairs gas exchange, and leads to air trapping and dynamic hyperinflation.

pmc-13520068.title: Evidence-based ergonomic parameters for safer surgical practice: a systematic review
pmc-13520068.creator: Jacqueline Wright, Erika Oki, Gonzalo Mariscal, Carlos Barrios
pmc-13520068.description: IntroductionWork-related musculoskeletal disorders are highly prevalent among surgeons and are primarily associated with sustained non-neutral postures, inadequate visualization, improper table height, and insufficient adaptation to individual anthropometry; therefore, this systematic review aimed to synthesize evidence on ergonomic risk factors and define evidence-based parameters for safer surgical practice.

pmc-13565052.title: Biomarkers in Gastric Cancer: Blood Biomarkers, Liquid Biopsy, Artificial Intelligence, and Risk-Stratified Care
pmc-13565052.creator: Helen D. Kim, Bryant Morocho, Elliott Lee, Steve Kwon
pmc-13565052.description: Simple SummaryDiagnosing gastric cancer early improves five-year survival from 8% to 78%. Endoscopy is accurate but too costly for universal screening in Western countries. This review examines whether simpler diagnostic tests/markers may help identify a high-risk group of people who may benefit from endoscopy.
